metadata.title: Meta upgraded, Nvidia initiated: Wall Street's top analyst calls

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
JPMorgan upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to Overweight from Neutral with a price target of $820, up from $640. The shares offer "meaningful upside potential" as Meta is in the early stages of releasing frontier models and AI-driven products beyond advertising, notably Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
Wells Fargo upgraded Synopsys (SNPS) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $475, up from $450. The firm says improving AI demand momentum and accelerating results into fiscal 2027 can drive the shares higher.
-
Wells Fargo upgraded Yum! Brands (YUM) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $175, up from $165. Despite a likely Q3 shortfall on uncertainty from Cyclospora, the shares offer a "compelling " long-term entry point, the firm says.
-
StoneX upgraded Block (XYZ) to Buy from Hold with a $105 price target. The output resulting from that agentic AI platform has been "impressive," while margin improvement is "the other significant dividend that Block has gained from its reorganization," the firm added.
-
Freedom Broker upgraded Caterpillar (CAT) to Buy from Hold with a $980 price target. The U.S. and Canada have entered a new phase of tariff escalation, notes the firm, which notes that Caterpillar does not have significant assembly operations in Canada.
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
Arete downgraded Uber (UBER) to Neutral from Buy with a $74 price target. Arete expects Uber's share overhang from autonomous vehicles to intensify.
-
Evercore ISI downgraded Chewy (CHWY) to In Line from Outperform with a $25 price target following what the firm describes as a "very modest beat & raise" fiscal Q2 EPS report. Organic growth has decelerated to 5.7% with the near- and medium-term outlook calling for more of the same, says the firm, which sees "little reason for the stock to outperform the market from here" without a clear catalyst or grounds to expect a fundamental inflection point.
-
William Blair downgraded Cooper Companies (COO) to Market Perform from Outperform following "two surprises" in last night's fiscal Q3 earnings report, namely a CooperVision miss due to inventory destocking and Cooper ultimately deciding not to sell CooperSurgical following its strategic review. BofA, Piper Sandler and Baird also downgraded Cooper Companies to Neutral-equivalent ratings.
-
JPMorgan downgraded United Rentals (URI) to Neutral from Overweight with a price target of $1,170, down from $1,235. The company is "best-in-class" given its "dominant" market share and margin profile, but the stock's valuation premium over peers reflects this, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
HSBC downgraded Amgen (AMGN) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $425, down from $445. After re-rating on Amgen's strong execution and positive estimate revisions, the stock is trading around fair value, the firm tells investors in a research note.
